proposedRoles.name: JM1 One Intake Runtime - Scoped
proposedRoles.rights: Create/read/write only the intake receipt, contact, lead, and exact parent-contact relationship operations listed in onePublicIntake. No Marketing Function, social publishing, catalog write, Assign, or administrative privileges.
proposedRoles.leadScope: Local candidate; the two child-BU rows do not establish a query need. The source uses deterministic request-derived IDs and no Lead-by-email search. Prove allowed exact-ID replay and safe denial on unrelated rows before adoption.
proposedRoles.contactScopeDecision: Unresolved. Option A: accept Deep Contact Read on the One MI, which exposes table-wide Contact rows and columns permitted by Dataverse; code-level $select is not an RBAC boundary and this does not guarantee email uniqueness. Option B: adopt a governed identity/dedup resolver or schema/key contract, then use Local Contact scope; policy must define shared-email/family cases and duplicate resolution, and no normalized-email unique key may be assumed until that contract is approved and deployed.

requiredPreCutoverProof: Create each MI application user separately; read back app ID/object ID, system user ID, business unit, enabled state, and exact role IDs.

For every operation/table/depth in approved matrices, run actual-caller allowed read/create/update/relationship tests against synthetic rows; verify the exact OrganizationOwned privilege union separately.

Run denied tests only for restrictions the selected role design can enforce. Do not claim target-specific Assign denial while broad Assign exists; omit Assign from One. Test Contact scope and unrelated Lead scope against the approved depth, Delete/Share and unlisted tables where the role actually denies them.

Run actual Function timer and One intake canaries using each host MI; prove durable receipt, safe replay, social read/write where applicable, bounded failure state, and logs free of private inquiry content.

Compare RetrieveUserPrivileges and actual record operations; reconcile indirect team/security-role access and field security. Retain prior shared authority until both workloads pass, then remove only its exact overbroad role through an independently verified rollback-ready change.

allowed: Natural timer read/write for each listed Function operation using its system-assigned MI; synthetic scoped row lifecycle; exact campaign and parent relationship bindings; queue and external-provider calls remain separately authorized.
denied: Unlisted Dataverse table; Delete/Share/Assign where absent from the proposed role; OrganizationOwned Create/Write on editorial gates and artifacts; UserOwned cross-BU records where Local depth is approved and the test record is owned outside HQ.
mustNotClaim: A timer/function-name boundary restricts table privileges.
Local execution-log scope guarantees future rows remain in HQ.
A denial of an out-of-scope owner target proves target-specific RBAC if Assign is granted.

allowed: Synthetic durable receipt create/read/update and safe replay; synthetic exact-email Contact lookup under the selected approved Contact depth; deterministic Lead create/read/update by request-derived ID; Lead-to-Contact binding.
denied: Unlisted tables; Delete/Share/Assign where absent; cross-BU Contact lookup only if Local Contact scope is selected; unrelated child-BU Lead reads if Local Lead scope is approved.
mustNotClaim: An unrelated Lead denial proves behavior for exact deterministic-ID collision cases.

actualCallerAcceptance.testData: Use isolated synthetic rows in DEV then Test, with known BU ownership and cleanup through the test harness. No real customer records, external sends, social posts, or held PRD/FIN routes. Capture principal/client ID, Dataverse system user, effective privileges, row owner/BU, request/response status, receipt ID, and safe log correlation without inquiry content.

perHostRollback.precondition: Before each single-host cutover, capture that host's current DATAVERSE_AUTH_MODE value, secret-reference metadata (never secret values), app configuration version, deployment SHA, and health/readback baseline. Preserve the other host unchanged.
perHostRollback.function: If acceptance fails, restore func-jm1-marketing-runtime to its captured prior client_credentials mode/unset state and unchanged existing Key Vault client references; restart/read back the Function, verify timer health and the existing shared principal, then reconcile queued work before any retry. Do not remove or change the shared Dataverse application user or its roles as rollback.
perHostRollback.oneWeb: If acceptance fails, restore app-jm1-one-prod-v2 to its captured prior client_credentials mode/unset state and unchanged existing Key Vault client references; restart/read back App Service health and synthetic intake receipt/replay using the existing shared principal. Do not change the Function host or remove the shared Dataverse application user or its roles.
perHostRollback.order: Cut over and validate one host at a time. Roll back only the failing host. Preserve prior app settings and release artifacts until both host-specific acceptance windows close.
